habitat: Anadromous schooling shad: adults live in open coastal waters and run up large rivers to spawn at night on shallow gravel beds; juveniles stay near estuaries for over a year. In the Gironde basin spawning grounds now lie within about 160 km of the ocean on the Dordogne and 300 km on the Garonne (MIGADO 2019).

size.maxNote: FishBase: max 83 cm TL for females (69 cm TL males/unsexed), not flagged as a record; common length 40 cm TL males/unsexed, 70 cm TL females. DORIS gives average 54 cm, max 80 cm.

diet: Adults mainly planktonic crustaceans, larger fish also small schooling fishes; juveniles in fresh water eat insect larvae (FishBase). Adults stop feeding once in fresh water (DORIS).
behaviour: Anadromous, schooling, strongly migratory; semelparous (most adults die after spawning, only about 4-6% spawn again). Spawns at night in noisy surface-splashing displays called 'bulls'.
seasonal: Gironde-Garonne-Dordogne: in 2019 MIGADO recorded the first spawning bulls on 25 April (water just above 12 C), with spawning spread over May-June. habitat: Anadromous bottom-dweller of mud and sand. Juveniles spend 3-7 years in the brackish Gironde estuary (zones deeper than 5 m, mean depth 4-8 m), feeding mainly on polychaete worms, then range widely at sea along the Bay of Biscay, Channel, North Sea and Irish Sea coasts, mostly shallower than 40 m (PNA 2011-2015).

size.maxNote: 600 cm TL and 400 kg historical maximum (FishBase); common 125 cm TL. DORIS: typically 1-2 m.

diet: Benthic invertebrates: polychaetes (main prey in the Gironde estuary), crustaceans such as gammarids, brown shrimp and green crab, molluscs, and small fishes; adults do not feed during the spawning migration.
behaviour: Anadromous, usually solitary and very long-lived (up to about 100 years). Males mature at 10-12 years, females at 13-16 years. Spawns over gravel and boulders in fast, deep water of the Garonne and Dordogne.
seasonal: Adults enter rivers January-October, peaking early April to late May; spawning in the Garonne-Dordogne mainly in May and early June. Estuarine juveniles move to the coast near the estuary plume in autumn-winter and back into the estuary in spring-summer, a movement called the 'Mouvee de la Saint-Jean' (PNA 2011-2015).
